base_member_text: [L21-L30] (MED/error-handling/reproducibility) The build and install pipeline has no failure checks or `set -e`, so failed cleanup, generation, configure, compilation, or installation can still be followed by module publication.
audit_member_text: [L13-L38] (HIGH/build-failure-propagation) Dependency loading and build failures do not stop installation or module generation, allowing a failed build to produce a published module.

adversarial.rationale: Unchecked build-to-publication fall-through exists when the H7 body is interpreted by Bash without errexit, but the stored file has CRLF on lines 1-39: ordinary direct Unix execution fails at the shebang before reaching any build. A correctly named published module requires line-ending normalization (or a CR-tolerant environment) and a usable module generator/input; raw Bash execution also appends a carriage return to the redirected module filename at line 38, so normal successful publication is not established for the raw file.

base_member_text: [L40] (LOW/permissions) The generated module file is made mode 777, granting unnecessary write/execute permissions to all users.
audit_member_text: [L40] (HIGH/shared-file-permissions) chmod 777 makes the installed shared environment module writable by every user, allowing accidental or unauthorized changes to other users' execution environment.
